citations.quote: MANILA, Philippines — Lawmakers have deferred approval of the proposed 2027 budget of the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT), in a bid to summon and force Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg to address violence and child safety concerns on Facebook.
At Wednesday’s plenary deliberations, the House suspended the DICT’s 2027 budget as they wanted Zuckerberg to face the agency during an inquiry into social media safety.

The House of Representatives deferred the consideration of the proposed budget of the DICT and its attached agencies following an interpellation concerning online safety, digital scams, and platform accountability.

The House of Representatives late Wednesday deferred deliberations on DICT proposed 2027 budget due to online safety issues.

MANILA, Philippines – The House of Representatives late Wednesday held off from further discussing the Department of Information and Communications Technology’s (DICT) proposed 2027 budget, as lawmakers flagged online safety concerns during floor debates on the agency’s spending plan.

Philreca party-list Rep. Presley de Jesus motioned that debates on DICT’s P10.68 billion be deferred as lawmakers would rather await the results of its efforts to curb harmful online content, crack down on scams and secure agreements with social media platforms.
Add to that a lingering concern over online scams, and the situation has brewed mounting frustration among lawmakers that ultimately prompted them to put on hold the DICT’s budget.

The House also deferred action on the proposed P19.49-billion budget of the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) and its attached agencies for 2027 pending resolution of issues involving Meta and online safety.
In addition, lingering concerns over online scams have fueled mounting frustration among lawmakers, prompting them to put on hold the DICT’s budget.

Presley de Jesus moved to defer the DICT’s proposed P10.68-billion budget to give the committee time to assess the results of the department’s crackdowns on the exploitation and sexual abuse of children, scams, cyberbullying and other concerns that put minors at risk.
The House majority bloc supported de Jesus’ motion to shelve DICT’s budget debates with no objections.

citations.quote: MANILA, Philippines – The House of Representatives on Wednesday, September 16, summoned Meta Platforms CEO Mark Zuckerberg to respond to concerns over child safety on its platforms.

The House also deferred action on the proposed P19.49-billion budget of the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) and its attached agencies for 2027 pending resolution of issues involving Meta and online safety.

The DICT, in a social media post on Wednesday evening, said the issues with Meta were related to the Online Sexual Abuse and Exploitation of Children (OSAEC) and Child Sexual Abuse and Exploitation Materials (CSAEM).
These were seen as “grave threats” demanding action and accountability.

In addition to the OSAEC and CSAEM issues, further harms were also being facilitated or amplified on major platforms, including online illegal gambling, cyberbullying, social media addiction, depression, and related mental health risks that might endanger Filipinos, especially the young.
The DICT added that Meta Platforms “continues to fall short of its responsibility and commitment to youth safety.”
The company’s scale and reach requires an obligation from them to set up proper safeguards, remove harmful content promptly, and cooperate with Philippine authorities.
The DICT, in its statement, said it would continue taking Meta to task for any missteps it makes, adding that “accountability cannot be optional.”

“The safety and welfare of Filipino children must remain paramount. Technology companies that operate in the Philippines must be held to the highest standards of responsibility. Persistent failure to address these risks erodes public trust and cannot be tolerated,” it added.

In a separate DICT post early on Thursday morning , the House of Representatives said it summoned Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg to face the DICT to respond to its concerns surrounding harmful online content and platform accountability, alongside hopefully setting up measures to improve online safety for Philippine users.

citations.quote: DICT/Facebook MANILA — Lawmakers are pressing for heavier platform accountability, prompting calls for Meta Chief Executive Officer Mark Zuckerberg to address the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) in a congressional inquiry centered on digital safety.

“The House of Representatives of the Philippines has called on Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg to face the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) during a House hearing on social media safety,” DICT said in its social media post.

According to the social media post shared by the DICT, the upcoming discussions will heavily focus on "concerns related to harmful online content, platform accountability, and measures to strengthen online safety for Filipino users."
PHILRECA party-list Rep. Presley De Jesus raised issues regarding harmful online content, child safety concerns, and misinformation following recent violent incidents.

“After the Ateneo de Zamboanga school shooting, DICT and CICC publicly raised the possibility of blocking Facebook as a last resort over delayed takedowns of violent content, child safety concerns, and misinformation,” De Jesus pointed out.
Llamanzares also said the department wrote to Meta’s CEO.
“Well, from the DICT, they themselves wrote directly to Mark Zuckerberg to ask him to confront these issues which we are facing. Although, there was no response.”

Citing the lack of visible, immediate results in curbing scams and protecting minors, De Jesus moved to defer the budget deliberations, a motion that was supported by the majority and formally approved by the leadership.
